ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Enzymes A and B are treated with the same protease, and the relationship between enzyme activity and treatment time is shown in the figure. What substance might enzyme A be?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is “enzyme activity,” and the horizontal axis is “time.” The curve corresponding to enzyme A basically remains horizontal, indicating that as protease treatment time is prolonged, the activity of enzyme A changes almost not at all; the curve corresponding to enzyme B decreases obviously as time is prolonged, indicating that the activity of enzyme B is gradually destroyed by protease treatment. Then reason: proteases mainly hydrolyze proteins. If the activity of enzyme A is still basically unaffected after protease treatment, this indicates that enzyme A is very likely not a protein enzyme; but it still has the catalytic function of an enzyme, so enzyme A may be RNA with catalytic function, namely a ribozyme.
